answers-lazy.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty of two thousand rows, abandoned, fifty times over. The inference pin is ZERO and that zero is the case: bridge.pl's metta_node_guarded/2 reports what a job spent as that job's LAST event, reached only once the command has no more answers, so an abandoned job contributes nothing. A lazy path that began draining would report query-rows' 282622 and fail this row by four orders of magnitude, and the workload's own crossing bound fails first at 1600. Instructions carry the SIZE, since a counter fixed at zero cannot say whether twenty rows cost twenty rows' work or two thousand; most of what they price is the teardown, because leaving the loop early closes the cursor and destroys the engine behind it. Fifty abandonments rather than one because a two millisecond window spread 0.2763 percent across nine samples against a one percent band. Inferences identical in all 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs; instructions spread 0.0399 percent over 9 samples of 3 consecutive runs [measured 2026-08-28: minimum of [815818054, 815831092, 815774521]; command=CHECK_PY=<an interpreter with janus_swi> sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build, box under loadavg 9 with another gate running; commit=0f6803e2377036ae526474434851b7a592f04703] RE-PINNED 2026-08-28 for a HARNESS fix, not a code change: every instruction row moved at once and every inference row stayed identical, which is the signature of the measurement rather than the work. benchmarks/sampler.ts now collects the heap to a fixed point at the end of setup, outside the window, under a fourth V8 flag `--expose-gc`. The three flags already there make a run reproducible against ITSELF; this makes it reproducible against a CHANGED PROGRAM. `--predictable-gc-schedule` is deterministic given the same allocation sequence and the startup heap is part of that sequence, so growing any module the benchmark loads shifted where a collection landed inside the window. Measured rather than argued, by a probe that cannot possibly do work: four kilobytes of INERT COMMENTS added to src/theory.ts moved host-op from 900018262 to 933434511, a 3.7 percent phantom regression from text nothing executes, and the same probe against the settled heap moves the whole suite at most 0.18 percent (atom-intern), with host-op at 0.016 percent. The rows that went UP now carry the collections their own allocation causes instead of inheriting an accidental share of the startup heap's, which is why answers-lazy and query-rows rose while host-op and atom-intern fell. This is the layout-bias class Mytkowicz et al. name, and a settled starting heap is the cheap half of Stabilizer's answer to it [source: Mytkowicz, Diwan, Hauswirth and Sweeney, "Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!", ASPLOS 2009; Curtsinger and Berger, "Stabilizer", ASPLOS 2013]. This row moved 814157514 to 1015712124 in that one step [measured 2026-08-28; command=sh extensions/node/bench.sh --update; fixture=swipl-wasm 8.0.6 on node 22.22.1 (V8 12.4.254.21-node.35), the compiled TypeScript build; commit=WORKTREE].

define-call.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Five hundred host calls of a lowered `define`d body, 477.01 inferences a call. The body is lowered, so the whole of it lives in the engine and a call costs no host crossing per step; what this prices is the per-call path, the ask out and the one answer back. Inferences alone decide, because the host's share is one ask per call and is already the smallest this door can be. counter_policy: stats().inferences minimum of three and fixed two-point growth slopes decide; wall time advises
counter_policy_note: Inferences decide wherever the engine does the work and are identical run to run; retired instructions decide where the work is on the TypeScript side of the wire, where the engine counter cannot move; three cases straddle the boundary and pin both. Wall clock decides NOTHING here and is recorded for advice only: every number in this file was taken on a box under loadavg 9 with another gate running, where the inference rows were byte identical across nine samples and wall clock was not.
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three, one percent noise allowance unless a row declares its own beside the measurement that justified it
v8_flag_note: Every instructions row is measured under the v8_flags in the stamp. A Node process is not deterministic enough to gate on retired instructions without them: bare, one engine workload spread 29.48 percent over four rounds, --liftoff-only alone took it to 2.55 percent and named the mechanism as TurboFan tiering swipl-wasm up on background threads inside the window, and the full set reaches 0.027 percent. These rows therefore measure Liftoff-compiled WebAssembly and single-threaded V8 rather than the tier a long-lived process settles into, which is the right trade for a gate that reads the change [measured 2026-08-28].
